title: Which loop does a node live in?
prompt: A toy graph has two kinds of node: Range(depth, name), a loop counter at nesting depth depth (1 is the outermost loop), and Op(name, srcs), where srcs is a list of nodes. Write depth(n: Node) -> int: the loop depth a node must be computed at, which is the deepest range it can reach through its sources, or 0 if it reaches none. Keep the classes and the function name as given.

tests.expr: (lambda i, j, k: depth(Op('add', [i, j])))(Range(1, 'i'), Range(2, 'j'), Range(3, 'k'))
(lambda i, j, k: depth(k))(Range(1, 'i'), Range(2, 'j'), Range(3, 'k'))
(lambda i, j, k: depth(Op('mul', [Op('add', [i, Op('const', [])]), Op('const', [])])))(Range(1, 'i'), Range(2, 'j'), Range(3, 'k'))
(lambda i, j, k: depth(Op('store', [Op('shrink', [Op('add', [Op('mul', [i, Op('c', [])]), j])]), Op('add', [Op('load', [k]), i])])))(Range(1, 'i'), Range(2, 'j'), Range(3, 'k'))
(lambda i, j, k: depth(Op('where', [Op('cmplt', [j, i]), i, Op('c', [])])))(Range(1, 'i'), Range(2, 'j'), Range(3, 'k'))

hints: A value has to be computed inside every loop whose counter it uses, and nowhere deeper. So its depth is the deepest range it can reach.
Recurse: a Range knows its own depth. An Op takes the maximum over its sources, and an op with no sources (a constant) is depth 0.
max(...) raises on an empty sequence. max((depth(s) for s in srcs), default=0) does the whole Op case.
explain: Depth is the maximum range depth reachable from a node, with constants at 0. In a real compiler you would memoize this on a shared DAG (each node visited once) and check that the ranges nest, but the rule is this one line.
